title: How I tell Claude what to change when I make a game (I'm not a programmer)
author: Accurate-Setting-357
selftext:
I wanted to share the loop I used to make Ink & Tide, a typing roguelite built entirely with Claude (Sonnet 5.5). I design, direct and test, and Claude does the code, the art and the music, so most of my job is deciding what the game should feel like and telling it clearly.

The loop is pretty simple. I plan the change in chat first and nothing gets built until I say yes. Then I describe each change in game words, meaning what it is, where it sits on the screen and what it looked like before, and I send two to five changes at once with a "change only these" so nothing else moves. Claude edits, I play the new version and report back what felt off.

For the art, every asset is drawn from the same style prompt sheet so the whole game matches, and the music comes from small synths that run in the browser. The thing that broke me a little was scope: combat got so complicated that I hid half of it for a later version and shipped the small one instead, which was the right call.

It's free to play here if you want to see the result: [https://jupitax.itch.io/ink-and-tide](https://jupitax.itch.io/ink-and-tide)

I'm still figuring out how to keep one art style across lots of AI-made assets, so I'd love to know how you handle it :)
